blocks.text:
Anthony Russell attacked Huntley with a metal bar while they were in a recycling workshop at HMP Frankland

A prisoner who bludgeoned the Soham killer Ian Huntley to death with a 4kg metal bar has changed his plea to guilty, one day into his murder trial.

Anthony Russell had admitted being responsible for the death of Huntley in HMP Frankland but denied murder on the grounds of diminished responsibility, instead pleading guilty to manslaughter. On Tuesday, he appeared at Newcastle crown court to change his plea to guilty of murder. The judge, Mr Justice Hilliard, said he would sentence Russell, 44, later that day.
